# Dream Counsellor

> An independent, free index of 220 funded programmes, scholarships, research
> placements and career routes open to Indian medical students and graduates.
> It is a static site with no account, no server and no tracking. Answering three
> questions produces a ranked plan; nothing is uploaded to produce it.

Dream Counsellor exists because most Indian medical students are handed one map
with two roads on it: clear NEET-PG, or leave for the USMLE. Both are real.
Neither is the whole territory. This index lists the funded research, the
doctorates that pay a salary, the scholarships that cover the flight, and the
scientific fields nobody mentions during five years of lectures.

## What it contains

- 180 opportunity entries: masters and doctorates, scholarships, fellowships,
  research studentships, conferences and practice-licensing routes
- 18 specialty route maps describing what each clinical specialty is really like
- 22 frontier fields: disciplines that exist and are hiring, and that Indian
  medical curricula do not mention
- 33 countries with at least one entry
- 41 entries that cost nothing to apply for or take part in
- A skip list of 8 things that look open to Indian medical students and are not

## How the content is organised

Every entry carries: the provider, the country, what it costs and what is funded,
how long it lasts, the application window, who it is open to, the steps to
approach it, and a link to the programme's own official page. Facts and
judgements are kept in separate files, so the impact grading of an entry can be
disagreed with without touching the underlying facts.

Entries are graded on a five-tier impact scale. Tier 1 is career-defining and
rare; tier 5 means do not build a plan on this. Most things are not tier 1 and
the site says so.

## Important pages

- [Dream Counsellor](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/): the index itself, with the three-question survey, the globe, browse, deadlines and shortlist
- [Open during MBBS](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/during-mbbs/): what a student can apply for before graduating
- [Studying abroad](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/study-abroad/): routes that accept an Indian medical degree
- [Scholarships](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/scholarships/): funded awards open to Indian applicants
- [Fellowships](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/fellowships/): research, global health and policy fellowships
- [Research opportunities](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/research/): studentships, summer programmes and grants
- [Inside India](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/india/): funded routes that need no visa
- [Fully funded](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/fully-funded/): entries where the provider covers the full cost
- [Costs nothing](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/free/): free courses, datasets, networks and memberships
- [Conferences](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/conferences/): meetings that accept student abstracts
- [Specialties](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/specialties/): 18 specialties, each with the day's work, the NEET-PG route, the superspecialities that follow, the routes to practising abroad, and the trade-off people leave out
- [Research fields](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/research-fields/): 22 active areas, what each one is, why India is under-represented in it, and one thing a student could start this week
- [Privacy](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/privacy.html): what is stored, and where
- [Terms of use](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/DREAMS/terms.html): including the accuracy caveat below

## How to treat the information here

Entries were last re-checked against their official pages in September 2026, and
that review date is rendered from data rather than typed into the page, so it
cannot quietly disagree with itself.

**Every deadline and amount here is a starting point, not the authority.** The
official page linked on each entry is the authority. Programmes move their dates
and change their rules; a confidently stated wrong date is worse than no date,
because someone who believes a call closed in January will not look again in May.
If this index and an official page disagree, the official page is right.

Eligibility is checked before an entry is added. Several widely recommended
programmes are deliberately excluded and named in the skip list because they
quietly exclude MBBS graduates, among them DAAD WISE, DAAD RISE, PMRF and the
Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships, none of which say so on their front page.

## What this site is not

It is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any institution listed.
It is not medical, legal, immigration or financial advice. It sells nothing,
collects nothing, and runs no advertising or analytics.
